text: A wave smashes over a Viking longship. On deck, the most famous helmet in history, with two big horns.
Except there's no proof a Viking ever wore one.
In 1943, a man in Norway dug into a mound to build a house, and found a Viking grave.
Inside was a real Viking helmet, in 9 pieces. Plain iron, an eye guard, no horns.
Horns would just get in the way in a fight.
The horns came from a German opera in 1876.
Costume designer Carl Emil Doepler put them on the helmets, and the look stuck.
Within about 25 years, horns meant Vikings.
The twist: horned helmets were real. Two turned up in a Danish bog in 1942. They're 2,000 years older than the Vikings.
